evidence.V1: Doorway reads from front, three-quarter and silhouette (opening punched through, centred); top view is a clean bar as expected for a wall module.
evidence.V2: Clear tiers: slab, cap ledge and plinth (big), block piers, lintel and door frame (medium), gold keystone (small).
evidence.V3: Sound proportions and a centred opening, but blocks are uniform rectangles and the frame is a thin flat band; partly stylised rather than confident.
evidence.V4: Consistent small chamfers on blocks, frame, threshold and cap ledge that catch light in the doorway, lintel and end close-ups.
evidence.V5: Doorway, lintel and end-section close-ups (studio and flat) show clean flat shading; no pinches, seams or z-fighting.
evidence.V6: Stone grey in about 3 values plus a single gold keystone accent; brick and basalt colourways keep the value structure.
evidence.V7: 540 tris vs module target 800, under target.
evidence.V8: One LF_VertexColor material, stone hue values, gold keystone accent and kit-scale chamfers; matches the modular kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct (anchored, Default collision keeps the doorway walkable, CanTouch off, white colour, grid-corner pivot); T1 tiling pass with iou 0.989.

artifacts: keystone slightly overhangs the lintel's lower edge into the opening (lintel close-up); reads as intended but borderline
top_fixes: Give the door surround more stylised weight: thicker projecting jambs/lintel or an arched head, with block-cut voussoirs
Vary pier block sizes and add a small tier (chipped corner, iron hinge pins in ink) for richer detail
Dress the exposed end section with block returns for wall-run terminations
